Hannah,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. HarborTech Legal reviewed and we have three priority items to confirm before we can proceed:

1) Output ownership: We need language that explicitly confirms HarborTech owns Customer Output produced by the Service (including model responses) and that Redwood will not assert ownership over customer output or derivatives.

2) Training/data use: HarborTech requires an opt-out for model training and derivative model improvements. If Redwood wants to use customer data for training, HarborTech will require a separate written license and a reasonable fee.

3) Feedback license: Any feedback HarborTech provides (bug reports, quality improvement suggestions) can be used by Redwood for support but must not be re-used to train models or improve general-purpose models without permission.

I've attached the HarborTech redline (Harbor-DRAFT-OrderForm_v2.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's standard approach and whether legal can accept these carveouts or propose alternative wording? We have a soft close target this week, so timeline is tight.

Best,

Forwarding HarborTech redline and Sara’s note. Quick asks from legal/product perspective:

Summary of HarborTech asks:
- Explicit customer ownership of all Customer Output (including model-generated text)
- No use of Customer Content for training/general model improvement without separate agreement
- Feedback limited to support/bug fixes; no training use

My suggested approach (commercial + legal tradeoffs):
- Offer an explicit training opt-out clause that prevents Redwood from using Customer Content or Output to train or improve our base models. Keep a narrow license to use the Customer Content and Output to provide the Service (e.g., troubleshooting, per-customer model tuning if requested and paid).
- Add anonymization and retention limits (e.g., 30–90 days) to mitigate data-sensitivity concerns.
- For feedback: propose a narrow feedback license that allows Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified feedback to improve service quality, but not to train general-purpose models; if HarborTech wants full prohibition, require concession on price/SLA.

Product questions for Markus: can we support a per-customer opt-out flag that prevents data from entering training pipelines (and how much lead time is needed)? Also: what are the operational costs we should flag to the customer?

Neha: please propose redline language we can send back. If this is commercial-impacting, flag to Priya (CPO) / Revenue for signoff — I’ll coordinate.

Quoted message below.

Thanks for the context — reviewed HarborTech’s redline and Hannah’s proposed approach. High-level legal position and recommended redlines below (draft language to follow in track-changes PDF):

1) Customer Output: Acceptable to confirm HarborTech owns Customer Output. We will add explicit language confirming customer ownership and a limited back-license to Redwood solely for providing the Service and for debugging issues related to HarborTech’s use. This preserves HarborTech’s ownership while allowing normal support operations.

2) Training/data use: Add an opt-out section — "Training Opt-Out" — that, if elected, prohibits Redwood from using Customer Content or Output to train or improve Redwood’s base models or shared models. Service functionality that depends on participation in training pipelines may be restricted; flag commercial impact. If HarborTech wants Redwood to use data for per-customer tuning, require a written license and scope.

3) Feedback license: Create a two-tier approach: (a) support/bug-fix feedback may be used internally; (b) product-quality feedback may be used in aggregated, de-identified form for internal product improvements but not to train public base models unless affirmative consent is given. If HarborTech requires a full prohibition, we will need a commercial concession.

Four asks of the team:
- Hannah: confirm whether HarborTech will elect the training opt-out and capture in the SOW/Order Form.
- Karthik/Markus: confirm implementation feasibility and expected ops cost.
- Hannah: schedule a call (Sara suggested Wednesday 11:00 PT) — I can join if legal is needed.
- If opt-out is elected: request Pricing provide estimated uplift; I will prepare the redline language for the Order Form and MSA references.

I will prepare track-changes and send in the next hour.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
